blocks.text: Managing your Slack workspace on Mac

Your Mac is the command center for your onboarding work. Slack is where you coordinate with your team to ensure clients get set up correctly. If you are on macOS 14 or higher, keep your Slack app updated to the latest version. This ensures you have access to the latest search modifiers and thread management tools. Use Command + / to pull up the full list of shortcuts. This is the fastest way to learn how to navigate your workspace without using your mouse.

items: Command + K: Open the quick switcher to jump to any client channel.
Command + F: Search within the current channel for specific onboarding notes.
Shift + Enter: Start a new line in a message without sending it.
Command + B: Bold your text to highlight important onboarding steps.

blocks.text: These shortcuts save you seconds every time you send a message. When you are onboarding ten clients at once, those seconds add up to hours. If you find yourself searching for the same client information repeatedly, try using search modifiers. Type from:@username or in:#channel-name to narrow down your results. This stops you from scrolling through months of history just to find one link.

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you stay in the flow. Instead of hunting through Slack menus, you can just ask Lazur to help. Hold your shortcut key and talk to find a specific message or draft a quick update to your team. It keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on your work.

Onboarding specialists often face a barrage of questions. It is easy to feel overwhelmed. Start by using the threads feature for every conversation. This keeps your main channel clean and ensures that specific client feedback does not get lost. If a question requires a long answer, reply in a thread. You can also use the save for later feature to mark messages that need your attention once you finish your current task.
If Slack starts to feel sluggish, use the built-in troubleshooting tool. Go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This often fixes performance issues that come from long-term use.

blocks.text: Integrating Slack with your other tools

You likely use a CRM like Salesforce or a project tool like Asana. Slack works best when you use it as a notification hub. Set up your integrations so that you get alerts when a client hits a milestone. Avoid the trap of keeping every channel open. Mute the channels that are not relevant to your current onboarding cohort. You can always check them later when you have a dedicated time block for general updates.

items: Sending sensitive client data in public channels.
Ignoring the threads feature and cluttering the main feed.
Not setting your status when you are in a deep work session.
Manually typing repetitive onboarding responses instead of using snippets.

blocks.text: Always double check which channel you are in before sending a message. A simple slip can send a private client note to a public channel. Use your status to let your team know when you are focused on onboarding tasks. This reduces the number of interruptions you get during your busiest hours.
Staying organized with Slack on Mac

Organization is a habit. At the end of every day, spend five minutes clearing your unread messages. Use the Unreads view to see everything you missed. If you cannot get to a message, mark it as unread so you remember to check it tomorrow. Your goal is to reach zero unread messages before you close your laptop. This gives you a clean slate for the next morning.

Lazur is not just for quick commands. It is for those moments when you need to find something on your screen fast. If you are looking at a long list of tasks in Slack, ask Lazur to point at the one you need. It saves you from scanning the screen yourself. It also helps you dictate messages when your hands are tired from typing all day. Keep your focus on the client, not the app interface.

faq.question: How do I jump to a conversation in Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: Press Command + K to open the quick switcher, then type the name of the channel or person.

faq.question: What is the best way to search for old messages?
faq.answer: Use Command + F in a specific channel or Command + G for global search. Use modifiers like from: or in: to narrow the results.

faq.question: How do I fix Slack if it is running slowly?
faq.answer: Go to the Help menu, select Troubleshooting, and click Clear Cache and Restart.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Slack?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur works in any app on your Mac. You can use it to dictate text, search, or get guidance on where specific buttons are located.
